page: Amazon Web Services c8i-flex.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It is configured with an x86_64 Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor operating at 3.9 GHz, providing 16 virtual CPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. Compute resources utilize a burstable allocation profile supported by an extensive 480 MB L3 cache. Vectorized execution and hardware acceleration are enabled through AVX-512, AMX tile, and AMX int8 instruction sets alongside AES and SHA cryptographic engines.

The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 system memory operating at 7 GHz, delivering an exact 1:2 allocation of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. No local storage is bundled with this instance type, requiring non-volatile storage to be mounted over the network. Network connectivity features a baseline throughput of 4 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default. Accelerated graphics hardware is absent, with GPU count standing at zero.

Benchmark data highlights strong single-core execution speed, evidenced by top 25 percent scores in Geekbench single-core, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression. Small-model LLM text generation ranks in the top 10 percent of measured servers, matching high text-processing throughput. In multi-threaded computational workloads, such as multi-core stress-ng tests, PassMark CPU benchmarks, and software compilation via Clang, the instance performs consistently within the middle 50 percent.

From an infrastructure cost efficiency perspective, the flex tier balances computational power and resource density by offering modern Intel architecture with burstable operational limits. This structure presents an efficient resource balance for workloads with variable execution demands, though organizations requiring sustained 100 percent utilization may observe throttle thresholds. Primary workload fits include batch job processing, Clang software builds, web serving, compression pipelines, and CPU-based lightweight AI inference.
